# 1 Clement Chapter 36 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_036_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 36

**36:1** This is the way, beloved, in which we found our salvation, Jesus Christ, the high priest of our offerings, the guardian and helper of our weakness.

**36:2** Through him we look steadfastly into the heights of heaven; through him we see as in a mirror his faultless and most excellent face; through him the eyes of our heart have been opened; through him our foolish and darkened understanding blossoms toward his marvelous light; through him the Master has willed that we should taste of immortal knowledge, since he is "the radiance of his glory, the exact imprint of his being, sustaining all things by the word of his power," at whose right hand the angels and archangels and powers and thrones and dominions are set, worshiping.

**36:3** Through the greatness and excellence of his beauty the six-winged and many-eyed ones stand before him, whom the seraphim and cherubim call, saying "Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord Sabaoth; full is the whole creation of his glory."

**36:4** And we also, being gathered in harmony in one place, let us cry out earnestly to him as from one mouth, that we may become partakers of his great and glorious promises.

**36:5** For it says: "Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and it has not arisen in the heart of man what things he has prepared for those who wait for him."

---

*EMET renders with maximal literalness. The christological description in v. 2 is among the closest parallels to the Epistle to the Hebrews in all of early Christianity (cf. Heb 1:3-4), using nearly identical language: "radiance of his glory, exact imprint of his being." Whether Clement quotes Hebrews or shares a common tradition is debated.*
